scope: One bounded 24-cell least-privilege model: three authority classes x eight interruption/authority events. The model tests worker-originated concurrency/rewind risk separately from repository-admin/owner lifecycle authority. No live branch policy, credential, repository, or scheduler mutation was performed.

observations: Fine-grained Contents(write) covers file-content writes and also Git ref create/update/delete endpoints, so Contents permission alone is not a non-rewind fence for a protected authority ref.

Fine-grained Administration(write) includes repository-level administration endpoints including DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}; separating Administration from worker credentials materially narrows destructive authority.
Expired or revoked tokens can no longer authenticate API or Git requests and cannot be restored; a replacement credential must be created.
Installation access tokens can be restricted to selected repositories/repository_ids and to permissions no greater than the App installation grants; installation tokens expire after one hour.

Get-a-repository is available with Metadata(read), while repository deletion requires administrative authority. The repository response exposes a repository id usable as a current identity field, but the reviewed public documentation does not establish that a same-repository stored expected id is a non-rewindable witness across owner-authorized delete/recreate.

authority_classes.least_privilege_worker: Worker has only the claim/effect content capability plus metadata read, has no Administration/ruleset/repository-lifecycle authority, is not an allowed branch-protection bypass actor, and every authority/effect transition uses current-blob CAS plus exact readback. Because generic Contents(write) can update Git refs, direct-ref safety additionally requires an already-current protection rule or an execution surface that does not expose raw ref mutation.
authority_classes.administrative_worker: Worker also possesses Administration or equivalent ruleset/repository-lifecycle authority; therefore privilege separation is absent even if its ordinary claim path still uses CAS.
authority_classes.repository_owner_lifecycle_authority: Actor can change repository policy/lifecycle or credential grants. This actor is explicitly outside the narrow worker-originated candidate threat model; uncertainty attributable to this authority must fail closed rather than be called safe.

aggregate.interpretation: Privilege separation removes the two structural meta-authority failures for the worker class: policy mutation and repository lifecycle mutation. It does not by itself make generic Contents(write) non-rewindable because Contents(write) includes Git ref update/delete endpoints; a current no-bypass protection rule or an execution surface that omits raw-ref writes is still required.

stable_repository_identity_fence.candidate: Bind each claim/effect attempt to the current repository id plus authority-blob SHA and policy epoch/expected protection state; reread identity and authority immediately before the authoritative effect and fail closed on mismatch, missing identity, policy uncertainty, 401/403/404, or rate limit.
stable_repository_identity_fence.works_for_narrow_worker_threat: Yes, because the least-privileged worker cannot itself delete/recreate the repository or edit the protection policy; identity/policy mismatches caused by out-of-scope lifecycle authority become a stop condition rather than a reason to accept stale state.
stable_repository_identity_fence.does_not_solve_owner_replacement: An expected repository id stored only inside the same repository is rewindable with that repository. The reviewed public docs do not provide a repository-local monotonic anchor that remains authoritative after owner-authorized delete/recreate. A selected-repository GitHub App installation may narrow access by repository_ids, but this run does not claim its grant/recreation semantics form an immutable anti-replacement witness, and provisioning/rebinding that grant would be an administrative action outside this CLEAN worker.

claim_idempotency_protocol.claim_transition: Read current authority object and current repository identity/policy evidence; write exactly one current-blob CAS transition; exact-readback after success or ambiguous response.
claim_idempotency_protocol.conflict: CAS conflict loses without side effect; do not retry blindly in the same invocation.
claim_idempotency_protocol.stale: Any stale authority blob, identity mismatch, policy mismatch, or old generation fails closed.
claim_idempotency_protocol.response_loss: Read deterministic claim/effect record before deciding whether another invocation may retry.
claim_idempotency_protocol.rate_limit: Checkpoint availability interruption; never interpret it as authority and never burn quota as compute.

observation_vs_inference.observed_from_docs: GitHub exposes separable Contents and Administration permissions; Contents(write) includes Git ref mutation endpoints, Administration(write) includes repository deletion, revoked tokens stop authenticating, and GitHub App installation tokens can be permission/repository scoped.
observation_vs_inference.model_inference: For cooperative recurring workers, keeping Administration/ruleset/lifecycle authority out of worker credentials plus current-blob CAS/readback and a no-bypass ref fence is sufficient to eliminate duplicate/conflicting worker-originated claim effects in the tested event set. The same design is not safe against an owner/admin who can alter policy, credentials, or repository lifecycle.
observation_vs_inference.scope_guard: This is a worker-originated concurrency/idempotency result, not an anti-admin-compromise or owner-lifecycle proof. It does not prove that the current connected credential is least-privileged or that required branch/ruleset policy is already configured.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.public_repository_free_scope: The Part121 predecessor already source-qualified public-repository branch protection/ruleset availability on GitHub Free. This leaf adds no hosted compute/storage credit mechanism; ordinary API rate limits are treated as availability interruptions and fail closed.
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: unresolved_for_acceptance: establishing or proving least-privilege credential grants and current no-bypass protection may require administrative configuration outside this CLEAN worker if not already present
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.paid_plan_independence_proven: only for the public-repository policy scope inherited from Part121; not generic private repositories

result.new_narrowing: The non-rewind requirement can be scoped away from ordinary recurring workers if their credential/tool authority excludes Administration/ruleset/repository-lifecycle mutation and the authoritative ref is protected from their generic Contents(ref-update) capability. Under those preconditions, current-blob CAS + identity/policy revalidation + exact readback handles stale claimants, concurrent claims, response loss, revocation, and rate limits without a second hosted coordinator. The remaining blockers are proving those least-privilege/protection preconditions without a manual/protected setup step and obtaining a non-rewindable repository-identity anchor for owner-authorized replacement.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: Can a Chat-native repository transport expose an already-enforced least-privilege worker capability boundary and stable repository incarnation binding as observable invariants, with no manual/admin provisioning step and no external monotonic witness, so the narrow worker-originated candidate becomes Phase-1-acceptable rather than merely conditional?

continuation: Part123: execute one bounded capability-surface invariant model. Compare (a) connected Chat repository tool surface that exposes only content-file CAS writes, (b) generic Contents(write) token with raw-ref endpoints, and (c) selected-repository GitHub App installation binding. Test whether capability introspection plus repository-id/install binding can prove, without admin/manual setup, that a worker cannot force-rewind, edit policy, or bind to a delete/recreated repository. Include token rotation/revocation and rate-limit fail-closed controls. If the installed capability boundary cannot be proven from Chat-native observable state, preserve it as the minimal unresolved child; persist one checkpoint and no second leaf.
